paragraphs.paragraph: The Revelation to Ezekiel in the Land of the Chaldeans
paragraphs.title: The Revelation to Ezekiel in the Land of the Chaldeans

easy.explanation: Ezekiel was among the captives by the river of Chebar.
easy.q: Where was Ezekiel when he saw the visions of God?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “the heavens were opened.”
easy.q: What was opened when Ezekiel saw the visions of God?

easy.explanation: Ezekiel saw a whirlwind come out of the north.
easy.q: What came out of the north?

medium.explanation: The passage identifies it as the fifth year of king Jehoiachin’s captivity.
medium.q: In what year of king Jehoiachin’s captivity did the vision occur?

medium.explanation: The KJV describes something like the colour of amber in the midst of the fire.
medium.q: What was seen in the midst of the fire?

medium.explanation: The opening description includes a whirlwind, a great cloud, fire, and brightness.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the beginning of the vision?

answers: He was among the captives when the vision came
He was serving in the temple
He was standing on a mountain
challenge.explanation: The passage gives both the time of the vision and Ezekiel’s location among the captives.
challenge.q: Which detail connects the timing of the vision with Ezekiel’s condition?

answers: That the revelation was accompanied by divine power
challenge.explanation: The expression indicates the Lord’s hand and presence were upon Ezekiel.
challenge.q: What does “the hand of the Lord was there upon him” indicate in the passage?

challenge.explanation: Fire and brightness appear at the beginning and are repeated in later descriptions.
challenge.q: Which feature appears in the opening description and is echoed later in the vision?

paragraphs.idea: The Revelation to Ezekiel in the Land of the Chaldeans

paragraphs.paragraph: The Four Living Creatures and Their Appearance
paragraphs.title: The Four Living Creatures and Their Appearance

easy.explanation: The passage describes four living creatures.

easy.q: How many faces did each creature have?

easy.explanation: Their appearance was like the likeness of a man.
easy.q: What was the general appearance of the creatures?

medium.q: How many wings did each creature have?

medium.explanation: The KJV specifically calls them straight feet.
medium.q: What does the description of “straight feet” emphasize?

medium.explanation: They had the hands of a man under their wings.
medium.q: What was under the wings of the creatures?

answers: A man, a lion, an ox, and an eagle
A man, a cherub, a lion, and a fish
An eagle, a horse, an ox, and a lion
challenge.explanation: The passage names the faces of a man, lion, ox, and eagle.

answers: The wings prevented them from moving
Their wings were joined, and they went straight without turning
The wings were used only to cover the wheels
challenge.explanation: Their wings were joined together, and they turned not when they went.
challenge.q: What was the relationship between the wings and the creatures’ movement?

answers: Each had all four kinds of faces
Each creature had only one different face
challenge.explanation: The text says that all four had the face of a man, lion, ox, and eagle.
challenge.q: What did the four creatures have in common concerning their faces?

paragraphs.idea: The Four Living Creatures and Their Appearance

paragraphs.paragraph: The Fire and Continuous Motion of the Creatures
paragraphs.title: The Fire and Continuous Motion of the Creatures

easy.explanation: Their appearance was like burning coals of fire and like lamps.
easy.q: What did the living creatures look like?

easy.explanation: The passage says that lightning went forth out of the fire.
easy.q: What came out of the fire?

answers: They moved in a slow circle
easy.explanation: The creatures ran and returned like a flash of lightning.
easy.q: How did the living creatures move?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes continuous movement in both directions.
medium.q: What does “ran and returned” describe in this passage?

answers: The lightning came out of the fire
The fire put out the lightning
The lightning was beneath the creatures
medium.explanation: The KJV says, “out of the fire went forth lightning.”
medium.q: What was the relationship between the fire and the lightning?

answers: They contributed to the creatures’ shining appearance
They were both inside the wheels
medium.explanation: The fire and brightness together emphasize the creatures’ radiant appearance.
medium.q: What quality did the fire and brightness share in the description?

answers: It presents them as lifeless objects
It emphasizes their brightness, heat, and power
It shows that they were made of stone
challenge.explanation: The burning coals, lamps, bright fire, and lightning emphasize their power and brilliance.
challenge.q: How does the description of fire help explain the appearance of the creatures?

answers: Both suggest light and rapid movement
challenge.explanation: The images communicate brightness and swift movement.
challenge.q: What do the images of lamps and a flash of lightning have in common?

answers: The creatures stand, the fire dies, and lightning appears
The creatures resemble fire and lamps, lightning comes forth, and they run and return
The creatures become wheels and disappear
challenge.explanation: This follows the order of the description in the passage.

paragraphs.idea: The Fire and Continuous Motion of the Creatures

easy.explanation: He saw one wheel upon the earth by the living creatures.
easy.q: What did Ezekiel see beside each living creature?

easy.explanation: The rings were full of eyes around them.
easy.q: What filled the rings of the wheels?

easy.explanation: The wheels went when the creatures went and were lifted when the creatures were lifted.
easy.q: How did the wheels move in relation to the creatures?

medium.explanation: The appearance and work of the wheels was like a wheel in the middle of a wheel.
medium.q: What does “a wheel in the middle of a wheel” describe?

answers: The spirit of the living creature
medium.explanation: The spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
medium.q: What directed the wheels in their movement?

answers: Move, stand, and be lifted up
medium.explanation: The wheels went, stood, and were lifted up with the creatures.
medium.q: What could the wheels do according to the passage?

challenge.explanation: The creatures and wheels moved in the direction they faced without turning.
challenge.q: What does the repeated statement that they “turned not” emphasize?

answers: The wheels were lifted when the creatures were lifted
The wheels always remained on the earth
challenge.explanation: When the creatures were lifted from the earth, the wheels were lifted also.
challenge.q: What was the relationship between the lifting of the creatures and the lifting of the wheels?

answers: The spirit of the living creature was in them
challenge.explanation: Their movement was connected to the spirit of the living creature within them.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the wheels did not move independently?

paragraphs.paragraph: The Firmament and the Sound of the Wings
paragraphs.title: The Firmament and the Sound of the Wings

easy.explanation: A firmament was above their heads.
easy.q: What was above the heads of the living creatures?

easy.explanation: It was like the colour of terrible crystal.
The noise of their wings was like the noise of great waters.
easy.q: What did the noise of the wings resemble?

medium.explanation: When they stood, they let down their wings.
medium.q: What did the creatures do with their wings when they stood?

answers: The voice of the Almighty and the noise of an host
The sound of a trumpet and the singers
The sound of rain and thunder
medium.explanation: The noise was compared to the voice of the Almighty and the noise of an host.
medium.q: Which additional sounds were compared with the noise of the wings?

medium.explanation: Their wings were beneath the firmament.

answers: The wings made noise when they went, and they let them down when they stood
The sound became louder whenever they stood
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the noise of the wings when they went and their being lowered when they stood.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between the creatures’ movement and the sound of their wings?

challenge.explanation: All three comparisons suggest a powerful and overwhelming sound.
challenge.q: What do the comparisons to many waters, the Almighty, and an host emphasize?

answers: From the firmament above their heads
challenge.explanation: A voice came from the firmament over their heads.
challenge.q: Where was another voice heard at the end of the section?

paragraphs.idea: The Firmament and the Sound of the Wings

paragraphs.paragraph: The Throne, the Human-Like Figure, and the Glory of the Lord
paragraphs.title: The Throne, the Human-Like Figure, and the Glory of the Lord

easy.explanation: The throne had the appearance of a sapphire stone.
There was the likeness of the appearance of a man upon it.
easy.q: What was upon the likeness of the throne?

easy.explanation: Ezekiel fell upon his face and heard a voice speaking.
easy.q: What did Ezekiel do at the end of the vision?

medium.explanation: The figure was surrounded by the appearance of amber, fire, and brightness.

answers: A rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day
medium.explanation: It was like the appearance of the bow in the cloud in the day of rain.
medium.q: What did the brightness around the figure resemble?

medium.explanation: The passage ends with Ezekiel hearing the voice of one that spake.
medium.q: What did Ezekiel hear after he fell upon his face?

answers: Firmament, throne, human-like figure, fire and brightness, then a voice
Voice, wheels, firmament, then a cloud
Fire, river, creatures, then a throne
challenge.explanation: This is the order of the vision in verses 26–28.
challenge.q: How does the vision develop from the firmament to the conclusion?

answers: The appearance of the brightness surrounding the figure
challenge.explanation: The brightness like a rainbow is identified as the likeness of the glory of the Lord.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “the likeness of the glory of the Lord” identify?

answers: Both include visions of God and a voice
challenge.explanation: The chapter begins with visions of God and ends with the vision followed by a speaking voice.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the beginning and the end of the chapter?

paragraphs.idea: The Throne, the Human-Like Figure, and the Glory of the Lord
